slides.title: Preserving muscle in MVA
slides.narration: This child has muscle wasting and mosaic variegated aneuploidy, a condition in which cells can carry different numbers of chromosomes. Our question is whether an existing medicine could improve muscle function while preserving the cells needed for growth and repair. We propose two medicines for laboratory testing.

slides.title: Protein supply is a testable mechanism
slides.narration: BUB1B makes the checkpoint protein BUBR1. Our stop-plus-missense pair matches a reported MVA1 pattern: reduced protein supply. The missense protein's stability and function remain unmeasured. Trans phase needs confirmation. Confirmed cis retires this pair as the compound-heterozygous explanation.

slides.title: Niacin tests usable protein restoration
slides.narration: Niacin is our lead because it targets the protein-supply hypothesis. It raised muscle NAD in another myopathy. Separate experiments connect NAD and SIRT2 to BUBR1 stability. Niacin has not rescued this genotype. We test whether it increases usable protein and useful muscle.

slides.title: Apitegromab tests muscle compensation
slides.narration: Apitegromab is our muscle-support comparator. It blocks myostatin activation and improved motor function in a randomized spinal-muscular-atrophy trial. It now has an approved use, but no MVA evidence. Fractures are a labeled risk. We test useful muscle output, without claiming that larger muscles repair the chromosome defect.

slides.title: Cell selection and tissue output
slides.narration: Our cell-selection explorer exposes a misleading result. In one simulated scenario, the chromosome-normal fraction rose sixteen point eight percentage points while total differentiated-cell time fell eleven percent. Other teams can inspect this tradeoff across declared assumptions. Our proposed experiment tracks starting cells, including those that die or stop dividing.

slides.title: The experiment must show useful muscle
slides.narration: We would compare affected and genetically corrected muscle models, using measured drug exposures. A medicine must improve either existing muscle or new muscle production, preserve the other, and avoid worsening chromosome errors. Independent confirmation must reproduce the result. The cancer history also requires checking that neither medicine helps tumor cells survive or interferes with cancer treatment.

slides.title: A broad search changed our comparison
slides.narration: Our public drug census screened over fifteen thousand clinical and regulatory entries. It made apitegromab a stronger downstream candidate than everolimus for muscle function. Everolimus remains a conditional signaling probe. Other same-gene genetic and drug findings have explicit limitations. Missing evidence stays unknown rather than becoming a failed drug.

slides.title: Public reuse and the next experiment
slides.narration: We also ran the workflow on a public, synthetic TRIP13 example. It shows why a BUBR1 restoration hypothesis cannot simply transfer to another gene. That demonstrates reuse, not treatment validation. Next we need a consented muscle model and laboratory partner to test niacin and apitegromab separately.
